checks.public_requirement: Each of the five files named above exists at the declared path directly under the output root (no extra directory layer), parses as a CSV with a header row exactly matching the declared header names in order, contains no duplicate header names, has uniform field counts in every data row, and contains only finite numeric values in each cell. open_closed_backbone_rmsd.csv must contain exactly one data row; the four trajectory tables must all have the same number of data rows.

The single data-row value equals, within max(|diff| <= 1e-5 angstrom, |diff|/reference-value <= 1e-6), the reference open-vs-closed backbone RMSD in angstrom for the atom populations, centering, weights and superposition defined in the question. The value must be non-negative.

Each data row has Frame exactly equal to its 0-based position (0, 1, 2, ...), Time (ps) equal to the reference frame time within 1e-6 ps, and Backbone, CORE, LID and NMP equal to the corresponding reference unweighted RMSD values in angstrom, each within max(|diff| <= 1e-5, |diff|/reference-value <= 1e-6). All RMSD cells must be non-negative.

Each data row has Frame exactly equal to its 0-based position (0, 1, 2, ...), Time (ps) equal to the reference frame time within 1e-6 ps, and the CORE column equal to the corresponding reference CORE alpha-carbon RMSD in angstrom within max(|diff| <= 1e-5, |diff|/reference-value <= 1e-6). The value must be non-negative.

Each data row has Frame exactly equal to its 0-based position (0, 1, 2, ...), Time (ps) equal to the reference frame time within 1e-6 ps, and C-alphas, CORE, LID and NMP equal to the corresponding reference mass-weighted RMSD values in angstrom (mass weights applied to every group in this table, per the question), each within max(|diff| <= 1e-5, |diff|/reference-value <= 1e-6). All RMSD cells must be non-negative.

Each data row has Frame exactly equal to its 0-based position (0, 1, 2, ...), Time (ps) equal to the reference frame time within 1e-6 ps, and C-alphas, CORE, LID and NMP equal to the corresponding reference resid-weighted RMSD values in angstrom (all atoms weighted by their residue id in every group, per the question), each within max(|diff| <= 1e-5, |diff|/reference-value <= 1e-6). All RMSD cells must be non-negative.

instruction:
## Acceptance addendum (AdK open⇄closed RMSD task)

**Compared artifacts.** Exactly the five CSV files named in the question, each read from the declared path directly under the output root (`outputs/<name>`; no extra directory layer). Files are parsed as comma-separated text with a single header row. The reference values are read dynamically from the reference copies of the same files.

**Row structure and identifiers.**
- `open_closed_backbone_rmsd.csv` must contain exactly one data row (its single column is a value, not a frame identifier).
- Each trajectory table must have one data row per trajectory frame; the four trajectory tables must all share the same row count. Row position encodes the frame: data row *i* must have `Frame` exactly equal to *i* (0-based), as a numeric cell equal in value to an integer. (The cell text may be `0`, `0.0` or any equivalent numeric spelling; the parsed value is compared.) Because `Frame` is a unique per-row identity, this rule is what makes frame misnumbering, row reordering, row omission, row duplication and appended extra rows fail.
- Every cell must be present, numeric and finite. Empty cells, non-numeric text, `nan`/`inf`/`-inf` and unequal field counts per row all fail. Negative RMSD values and negative times fail as invalid scientific results (RMSD is a non-negative deviation; time values here are positive).

**Headers.** The header must equal, in order and spelling: `backbone_rmsd_angstrom` for output 1; `Frame, Time (ps), Backbone, CORE, LID, NMP` for output 2; `Frame, Time (ps), CORE` for output 3; `Frame, Time (ps), C-alphas, CORE, LID, NMP` for outputs 4 and 5. Duplicate header names are not allowed. `Time (ps)` is compared as the reader's picosecond frame time (identical across the four tables; see below).

**Numeric comparison of RMSD values (Å).** Every non-identifier numeric cell (all RMSD columns, and the scalar in output 1) is compared to the corresponding reference cell, aligned by (file, row, column). A cell passes if either
- its absolute difference from the reference value is at most **1e-5 Å**, or
- its relative difference is at most **1e-6** of the reference value (reference cell is the denominator).

This is a limit on observable output differences. It is not a claim that every wrong method is detected, and rejection has not been tested arbitrarily close to the boundary. Executed negative controls demonstrate rejection for a mis-scaled scalar, swapped domain columns within a table, wrong-population values substituted from another file's table, coarse timestamp grids and coarse value rounding. Divergences between the weighting conventions themselves are far larger than the bound on this data — comparing the trajectory's own convention tables value-for-value, unweighted-versus-mass-weighted differences reach about a tenth of an ångström, and mass-versus-resid-weighted differences reach a few ångström — so a genuine convention error moves cells three to five orders of magnitude beyond the bound. Zero values and near-zero frame-0 residuals are compared through the same absolute branch and never rounded away; non-finite and negative cells are rejected outright, so NaN cannot make a failure disappear.

**Representation and precision.** Only decoded numeric values are compared, never text spellings or float widths: a full-precision `%e`-style scientific-notation rendering of the same values passes, as does `0` in place of `0.0`, and integer spellings for the `Frame` column. The submission's writer is still required to print at least 12 significant digits for non-integer values; the grader enforces this only through its value comparison — coarse rounding is rejected exactly when it moves a compared cell beyond the limits above. On this data, rounding to five significant digits moves most cells beyond the limits and is rejected (executed control on real frame data); rounding to six significant digits moves fewer cells beyond the limits and is therefore not a reliably rejected deviation. The digits requirement remains a formatting obligation on the writer, not an independent digit-string check in the grader.

**Time column (ps).** Compared with a tighter absolute bound: a time cell passes if its absolute difference from the reference cell is at most **1e-6 ps**. Frame times are identical across all four trajectory tables (cross-file consistency: the value for a given frame is the same quantity wherever it appears); a submission whose tables disagree in time will fail wherever the reference value is not reproduced. `Time (ps)` replicates the trajectory reader's reported time (the first frame's time reflects the file's saved time origin).

**Cross-file relations.** Row alignment is by (file, row = frame index). RMSD columns carrying the same name in different files are different physical quantities (different reference groups, weights and superpositions): each file is compared only against its own reference copy at the corresponding row, so substituting another table's same-name values fails wherever those values differ beyond the stated tolerance (an executed control demonstrates exactly this failure mode for a cross-file wrong-population substitution). Coverage is row- and column-complete for every table: missing rows, missing columns, extra columns, or extra appended rows (even well-formed ones) fail.

**Values compared, per output.**
1. `open_closed_backbone_rmsd.csv`: one backbone RMSD in Å between trajectory frame 0 and the open-conformation coordinates, after centering on the centers of geometry and optimal unweighted superposition.
2. `backbone_rmsd.csv`: per-frame unweighted RMSDs of the whole backbone and of the CORE/LID/NMP backbone subgroups after the backbone superposition onto frame 0.
3. `core_ca_rmsd.csv`: per-frame unweighted RMSD over the CORE alpha-carbons, superposition determined by those atoms.
4. `mass_weighted_rmsd.csv`: per-frame mass-weighted RMSDs (C-alphas from the `protein and name CA` superposition; domain subgroups also mass-weighted).
5. `resid_weighted_rmsd.csv`: per-frame RMSDs with all weights equal to atom residue ids (superposition and `C-alphas` from protein alpha-carbons weighted by resid; domain subgroups weighted by resid).

**Grader operation.** The grader exits 0 and writes a JSON report with one entry per declared check. Missing files, malformed content, non-finite values, wrong headers, wrong row counts and out-of-tolerance values each fail the affected scientific check(s) rather than crashing the grader. No paths, timestamps or environment variables other than the supplied reference/submission/report arguments are used.
probe_concerns: Time-column boundary: the reference Time values are full round-trip serializations of reader-reported times that reflect a float32-derived dt (first frame ~1 ps from the DCD's saved time origin; per-frame spacing drifts at the ~1e-6 ps scale). The 1e-6 ps absolute bound therefore sits near the scale of representable timing noise, and a solver recomputing times as exact integer-frame steps instead of reader-reported values could approach the bound at late frames. The public text prescribes 'as reported by the trajectory reader', and the executed uniform +5e-6 ps shift and the 1e-5 ps grid-rounding probes both fail through the time rule, but the boundary itself is not exercised by a genuine independent time recomputation against only saved reference values.

Depth limitation of the reference artifacts: the reference outputs contain only per-frame aggregates, not per-atom coordinates, selection indices or weight vectors, so probes can challenge the stated public rules (cell values, tolerances, cross-file column relations, representation format) but cannot validate the weighting/QCP superposition itself beyond value equality. This is an unavoidable evidence limitation of a representation-level validation suite, not a defect of the contract.

Weighting-convention negative coverage is not exercised by any executed probe. The two probes named for it (mass-weighted-to-unweighted, resid-weighted-to-mass-weighted) as frozen read the other file's values only for assertion counters and write each target cell back as a '%.17g' reformatting of its own value, which round-trips float64 exactly; their executed files are decoded-value-identical to the reference and are correctly annotated valid_alternative. Their scripts never perform the intended cross-convention substitution, so a genuine weighting-convention error (for example unweighted values written into the mass-weighted table) has no executed negative control in the recorded suite; the mass_weighted_rmsd and resid_weighted_rmsd rules retain wrong-result coverage only through the executed five-significant-digit rounding and time-grid probes, which are value-coarsening errors rather than convention errors.

probe_expectations.name: open-closed-scaled-one-percent
probe_expectations.rationale: The unchanged script rewrites only the single RMSD value in open_closed_backbone_rmsd.csv, preserving the exact header line, the single data row and a positive finite numeric cell, so every structural requirement of the public contract (declared path, exact header spelling, exactly one data row, finite numeric value) remains satisfied and the structural_schema check must pass. The original check_ids annotation contradicted the probe's own frozen rationale, which states that structural_schema still passes and the failure is purely scientific, and the executed grading record, in which structural_schema passed and only open_closed_backbone_rmsd failed. The wrong_solution classification is unchanged: the 0.1% inflation (about 0.0068 angstrom, relative 1e-3) exceeds both tolerance branches of the scientific rule while the file stays well formed. This probe remains the executed wrong-result coverage for the open_closed_backbone_rmsd scientific check.

probe_expectations.name: backbone-lid-nmp-column-swap
probe_expectations.rationale: The unchanged script swaps only the LID and NMP cell values within each row of backbone_rmsd.csv, keeping the six-field structure, exact header, row count, Frame identities, Time values and finite non-negative cells, so the file remains structurally valid and structural_schema must pass — as the probe's own frozen rationale states ('the file stays structurally valid ... so the failure targets the intended scientific rule rather than a parse cascade') and as the executed record shows (structural_schema passed; only backbone_rmsd failed). The original check_ids annotation wrongly listed structural_schema among the checks this mutation violates. The scientific target is unchanged: the swapped domain values differ from the reference beyond both tolerance branches in 97 of 98 rows, so the backbone_rmsd check must fail and retains its executed wrong-result coverage through this probe.

probe_expectations.name: core-ca-backbone-pool-contamination
probe_expectations.rationale: The unchanged script replaces only the CORE column values of core_ca_rmsd.csv, preserving the three-field structure, exact header, row count, Frame alignment and Time cells, so the file stays structurally valid and structural_schema must pass — as the probe's own frozen rationale states ('while Frame alignment, Time and the 3-column structure are preserved, so structural_schema still passes') and as the executed record shows (structural_schema passed; only core_ca_rmsd failed, on genuine cross-file wrong-population values). The original check_ids annotation wrongly listed structural_schema among the checks this mutation violates. The correction restores consistency between the check list and the mutation actually performed; the core_ca_rmsd scientific check keeps its executed wrong-result coverage through this probe.

probe_expectations.name: time-shift-plus-five-e-minus-six
probe_expectations.rationale: The unchanged script modifies only the Time (ps) cells (adding exactly +5e-6 ps) in the four trajectory tables, leaving headers, row counts, Frame identities, RMSD values, finiteness, positivity and cross-file time identity intact, so the files remain structurally valid and structural_schema must pass — as the probe's own frozen rationale states ('all RMSD values and Frame/row structure are untouched so structural_schema passes') and as the executed record shows (structural_schema passed; exactly the four trajectory scientific checks failed on the 1e-6 ps time rule). The original check_ids annotation wrongly listed structural_schema among the checks this mutation violates. The mutation is a genuine wrong result on real frame data: every time cell exceeds the 1e-6 ps absolute bound by 5x, so all four trajectory scientific checks fail and retain their executed wrong-result coverage through this probe.

probe_expectations.name: time-round-to-half-microsecond-grid
probe_expectations.rationale: The unchanged script rounds only the Time (ps) cells to a 1e-5 ps grid in the four trajectory tables, leaving headers, row counts, Frame identities, RMSD values, positivity and cross-file time identity intact, so the files remain structurally valid and structural_schema must pass — as the probe's own frozen rationale states ('all RMSD values and Frame identities are byte-identical ... and the script exits 0 with an actual mutation') and as the executed record shows (structural_schema passed; exactly the four trajectory scientific checks failed, 78 of 98 rows exceeding the 1e-6 ps bound). The original check_ids annotation wrongly listed structural_schema among the checks this mutation violates. The mutation is a genuine wrong result (a coarse timestamp grid instead of reader-reported times), so the four trajectory scientific checks fail and keep their executed wrong-result coverage through this probe.

probe_expectations.name: cells-rounded-to-five-sig-digits
probe_expectations.rationale: The unchanged script rewrites every data cell of all five files at five significant digits, keeping the files parseable with exact headers, uniform field counts, finite non-negative values, one row per frame and correct Frame identities, so structural_schema must pass — as the probe's own frozen rationale states ('the files stay parseable, finite, non-negative, with exact headers, row counts and Frame identities (structural_schema passes)') and as the executed record shows (structural_schema passed; all five scientific checks failed). The original check_ids annotation wrongly listed structural_schema among the checks this mutation violates. The mutation is a genuine wrong result: on real frame data the rounded scalar, many RMSD cells and most time cells move beyond the stated tolerance branches, so all five scientific checks fail and retain their executed wrong-result coverage through this probe.

probe_expectations.name: mass-weighted-to-unweighted
probe_expectations.rationale: The unchanged script does not perform the substitution its original rationale and wrong_solution label describe. It reads backbone_rmsd.csv only for header and row-count assertions; its rewrite loop writes each original cell of mass_weighted_rmsd.csv back as '%.17g' of its own parsed value, and 17 significant digits round-trip binary64 floats exactly, so the mutated file is decoded-value-identical to the reference copy with the correct header, row count, Frame identity and Time values. Under the unchanged public rules — decoded numeric values compared with the stated tolerances, and representation-preserving reformattings accepted (as the executed full-precision-e-notation control establishes) — the grading of this content must pass both listed checks, which is what the recorded execution shows. The original mistake was labeling the probe by its intended scientific challenge (a cross-convention substitution) rather than by the mutation the frozen script actually executes; that intended substitution would indeed fail, since the unweighted and mass-weighted convention tables differ beyond both bounds in 388 of 392 RMSD cells with differences up to about 0.1 angstrom, but it is not the content the script writes, so the wrong_solution annotation misdescribed the executed mutation.

probe_expectations.name: resid-weighted-to-mass-weighted
probe_expectations.rationale: The unchanged script uses the mass_weighted_rmsd.csv values only to compute an assertion counter (n>=380) and writes each original cell of resid_weighted_rmsd.csv back ('%.17g' of its own parsed value for the RMSD columns, original text for Frame and Time). Seventeen significant digits round-trip binary64 floats exactly, so the written file preserves every decoded value, header, row count, Frame identity and Time cell of the reference copy. Under the unchanged public rules the grading of this content must pass both listed checks, which is what the recorded execution shows. The original mistake was again labeling the probe by its intended scientific challenge rather than by the executed mutation: the intended mass-for-resid substitution would fail (the two convention tables differ beyond both bounds in 388 of 392 RMSD cells with differences up to a few angstrom), but the frozen script never writes those substituted values, so the wrong_solution annotation misdescribed what was actually graded. Wrong-result coverage for this check remains provided by the executed five-significant-digit rounding and time-grid probes, which do mutate the file's values.

rationale:
DIAGNOSIS OF THE REJECTION. The controller's executable control requires, for every wrong_solution probe, that each check listed in its check_ids fails the mutated submission (and, for a valid_alternative probe, that the listed checks pass). All eight wrong_solution probes in the frozen suite carry structural_schema in their check_ids, yet every frozen probe script deliberately preserves CSV structure (exact headers, uniform field counts, one row per frame, Frame identity, finite non-negative values) — each probe's own frozen rationale says so explicitly ('structural_schema still passes', 'the file stays structurally valid', 'so structural_schema passes') — and every executed grading run shows structural_schema passing. The check_ids annotations were therefore internally inconsistent with the frozen scripts and the executed records; no grader change could ever satisfy them. This is precisely the sanctioned annotation correction: a changed file need not violate all associated checks, and the fix is to correct the annotation, not the grader.

CORRECTIONS MADE (grader code, addendum, tolerances and check inventory are all unchanged; instruction and grader_code were returned as null/preserved). (1) For the six wrong_solution probes that genuinely mutate values (open-closed-scaled-one-percent, backbone-lid-nmp-column-swap, core-ca-backbone-pool-contamination, time-shift-plus-five-e-minus-six, time-round-to-half-microsecond-grid, cells-rounded-to-five-sig-digits), check_ids are corrected to drop structural_schema and list only the scientific checks the mutation actually violates. The executed records confirm exactly those scientific checks fail: the scaled scalar fails open_closed_backbone_rmsd; the LID/NMP swap fails backbone_rmsd; the cross-file population substitution fails core_ca_rmsd; the +5e-6 ps time shift and the 1e-5 ps grid rounding each fail all four trajectory scientific checks through the 1e-6 ps time rule; the five-significant-digit rounding fails all five scientific checks (the scalar exceeds both tolerance branches, many RMSD cells exceed them, and most time cells exceed the time bound, as I re-measured locally on the reference copies before the first submission). Every scientific check therefore retains executed wrong-result coverage, and structural_schema — which is not a scientific check — retains suite-level negative coverage through the executed empty, misplaced and five missing-file controls. (2) The two weighting-convention probes retain their corrected valid_alternative classification with unchanged check_ids: their frozen scripts write each cell back as a '%.17g' reformatting of its own value, which round-trips binary64 exactly, so the executed files are decoded-value-identical to the reference and both listed checks pass, as the executed records show. The still-open scientific gap (no executed probe performs a true cross-convention substitution) is recorded verbatim in probe_concerns rather than hidden, because the probe scripts are frozen and cannot be rewritten from this role.

EVIDENCE BASIS. All claims are grounded in the executed control records (probe before/after hashes, grader reports and per-check outcomes), byte-level reading of the frozen probe scripts, and my own measurements on the reference copies (five- and six-significant-digit rounding cell counts, convention-table divergences of up to ~0.1 and ~3.5 angstrom, structural rejection behavior of frame-shifted, shuffled, row-duplicated and wrongly-headed tables). No tolerance was widened or narrowed, no acceptance rule changed, and no check description, id, kind or artifact coverage was altered. The addendum from the previous submission is preserved exactly; it already restricts its rejection claims to the executed controls and cites the measured convention divergences.
